mechanism_narrative: The recent sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC, indicating a gradual return to pre-pandemic activity levels, will continue over the next four weeks, driving further increases in retail and recreation mobility.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant and sustained recovery in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, indicating increased essential outings, will spill over into non-essential retail, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as people combine errands.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM sustains above -5% from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains above -5% for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp decline in WORKPLACES mobility combined with a rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests a shift to remote work, which will suppress weekday retail and recreation activity, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the previous 28 days, despite WORKPLACES falling and RESIDENTIAL rising.

mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp drop in TRANSIT mobility, if sustained, indicates tightening public health measures or increased public apprehension, which will directly deter visits to retail and recreation venues, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30% from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains below -30% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not decrease over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: As colder weather approaches, indicated by sustained low PARKS mobility and high RESIDENTIAL mobility, people will seek indoor activities, potentially shifting some recreation to indoor retail venues, leading to a slight increase in RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -55% and RESIDENTIAL above 10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 7 days despite PARKS remaining low and RESIDENTIAL remaining high.

mechanism_narrative: The strong and consistent recovery in GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests a broader increase in public confidence for out-of-home activities, which will positively influence RETAIL_REC, driving it higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM continues its upward trend (week-on-week increase)
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise, but RETAIL_REC falls over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp one-week drop in WORKPLACES mobility is a temporary fluctuation; a quick rebound in workplace attendance will stimulate associated retail and recreation activity, leading to an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES recovers by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers by more than 5 points, but RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with declining TRANSIT usage indicates a strong preference for staying home and avoiding public transport, which will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 11% and TRANSIT remains below -30% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining high and TRANSIT remaining low.
